subproblem.title: Localization of integrals of functions continuous on an open set and vanishing off a compact subset
subproblem.statement: Let n be a natural number; integrals are Bochner integrals for Lebesgue measure on R^n. Let f : R^n -> R, and let O and T be subsets of R^n such that O is open, T is compact and T is contained in O. Assume that f is continuous on O (as a map restricted to O) and that f(z) = 0 for every z not in T. Then (a) f is continuous on all of R^n, (b) f is Lebesgue integrable on R^n, and (c) the integral of f over O equals the integral of f over R^n.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (f : Rn n → ℝ) (O T : Set (Rn n)), IsOpen O → IsCompact T → T ⊆ O → ContinuousOn f O → (∀ z, z ∉ T → f z = 0) → Continuous f ∧ Integrable f ∧ ∫ z in O, f z = ∫ z, f z
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 3c of the parent proof (the lemma stated there), written out in full. Let mu denote Lebesgue measure on R^n (MeasureTheory.volume); all integrals are Bochner integrals for mu.
1. T is closed. R^n is a Hausdorff space, so the compact set T is closed (IsCompact.isClosed). Hence the complement of T is open.
2. Continuity at points of O. Let z be in O. Since O is open, O is a neighbourhood of z (IsOpen.mem_nhds), so the continuity of f on O gives continuity of f at z (ContinuousOn.continuousAt).
3. Continuity at points outside O. Let z be outside O. Then z is not in T, because T is contained in O. By step 1, the complement W of T is an open neighbourhood of z, and f(w) = 0 for every w in W by hypothesis. So f agrees with the constant function 0 on a neighbourhood of z, and f is continuous at z (continuousAt_const.congr applied to this eventual equality).
4. Claim (a). By steps 2 and 3, f is continuous at every point of R^n, hence continuous (continuous_iff_continuousAt). Equivalently: tsupport f is contained in the closed set T, hence in the open set O, and ContinuousOn.continuous_of_tsupport_subset applies.
5. Compact support. f(z) = 0 for every z outside the compact set T, so the support of f lies in T and its closure tsupport f lies in the closed set T. Hence tsupport f is a closed subset of a compact set, i.e. f has compact support (HasCompactSupport.intro).
6. Claim (b). A continuous function with compact support is integrable for every measure that is finite on compact sets, and Lebesgue measure is such a measure. So f is integrable (Continuous.integrable_of_hasCompactSupport, using steps 4 and 5).
7. Claim (c). If z is not in O, then z is not in T, since T is contained in O; so f(z) = 0. Thus f vanishes on the complement of O, and the integral of f over O equals the integral of f over R^n (setIntegral_eq_integral_of_forall_compl_eq_zero).
8. Steps 4, 6 and 7 prove (a), (b) and (c). QED.
proof_key_steps: T is compact in the Hausdorff space R^n, hence closed
f is continuous at each point of the open set O; a point outside O lies in the open complement of T, where f = 0, so f is continuous there too
f vanishes outside the compact set T, so it has compact support and, being continuous, is integrable
f vanishes outside O, so its integral over O equals its integral over R^n

audit.reason: The one-line proposition exactly matches the prose and includes every hypothesis. Closedness of T supplies the zero neighbourhoods outside O; continuity inside O uses openness. Support containment yields compact support and integrability, and vanishing outside O gives the integral identity. All three conclusions follow without circular reliance, including when T is empty.

subproblem.title: Uniform convergence of the perturbed bilinear pairings and of the error forms on a bounded set
subproblem.statement: Let n, l be natural numbers. Notation: L := L(R^n, R^l), the continuous linear maps R^n -> R^l with the operator norm; L* := continuous linear forms on L; Bil := continuous bilinear forms on L, viewed as continuous linear maps L -> L*, written b[P][Q]; |z|^alpha is the real power (Real.rpow). Let alpha >= 0, r, Z and N be real numbers, A in Bil, ah_k : R^n -> Bil, Psi_k : R^n -> L*, U_k : R^n -> L (k in N), V, Q : R^n -> L, K an arbitrary subset of R^n, and c_k, d_k real sequences. Assume: c_k -> 0 and d_k -> 0; U_k -> V uniformly on K; |z| <= r, ||Q(z)|| <= Z and ||V(z)|| <= N for every z in K; for all sufficiently large k, all z in K and all P, P' in L: |ah_k(z)[P][P'] - A[P][P']| <= c_k (1 + |z|^alpha) ||P|| ||P'||; and for all sufficiently large k, all z in K and all P in L: |Psi_k(z)[P]| <= d_k |z|^alpha ||P||. Then, as k -> infinity, (i) the maps z -> ah_k(z)[U_k(z)][Q(z)] converge to z -> A[V(z)][Q(z)] uniformly on K, and (ii) the maps z -> Psi_k(z)[Q(z)] converge to the zero function uniformly on K.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (α r Z N : ℝ) (A : (Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn ℓ) →L[ℝ] (Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn ℓ) →L[ℝ] ℝ) (ah : ℕ → Rn n → (Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn ℓ) →L[ℝ] (Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn ℓ) →L[ℝ] ℝ) (Ψ : ℕ → Rn n → (Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn ℓ) →L[ℝ] ℝ) (U : ℕ → Rn n → (Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn ℓ)) (V Q : Rn n → (Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn ℓ)) (K : Set (Rn n)) (c d : ℕ → ℝ), 0 ≤ α → Tendsto c atTop (𝓝 0) → Tendsto d atTop (𝓝 0) → TendstoUniformlyOn U V atTop K → (∀ z ∈ K, ‖z‖ ≤ r) → (∀ z ∈ K, ‖Q z‖ ≤ Z) → (∀ z ∈ K, ‖V z‖ ≤ N) → (∀ᶠ k in atTop, ∀ z ∈ K, ∀ P P' : Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn ℓ, |ah k z P P' - A P P'| ≤ c k * (1 + ‖z‖ ^ α) * ‖P‖ * ‖P'‖) → (∀ᶠ k in atTop, ∀ z ∈ K, ∀ P : Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn ℓ, |Ψ k z P| ≤ d k * ‖z‖ ^ α * ‖P‖) → TendstoUniformlyOn (fun k z => ah k z (U k z) (Q z)) (fun z => A (V z) (Q z)) atTop K ∧ TendstoUniformlyOn (fun k z => Ψ k z (Q z)) (fun _ => (0 : ℝ)) atTop K
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 4 and 5a-5c of the parent proof. These are the pointwise error-term and main-term estimates on Bbar_r(0) with Q = Dzeta. Here they are stated for a general set K with explicit bounds. The supremum s_k of step 5b is replaced by the equivalent epsilon form of uniform convergence. Uniform convergence of maps F_k : R^n -> R to F on K means: for every eps > 0 there is k0 such that |F(z) - F_k(z)| < eps for all k >= k0 and all z in K (Metric.tendstoUniformlyOn_iff). The same holds for L-valued maps, with the operator norm.
1. Nonnegative constants. Put r0 := max(r, 0), Z0 := max(Z, 0) and N0 := max(N, 0); all three are >= 0. Let z be in K. Then 0 <= |z| <= r <= r0. Since t -> t^alpha is monotone on [0, infinity) for alpha >= 0 (Real.rpow_le_rpow), |z|^alpha <= r0^alpha. Also |z|^alpha >= 0 and r0^alpha >= 0 (Real.rpow_nonneg). Finally ||Q(z)|| <= Z <= Z0 and ||V(z)|| <= N <= N0. Using r0, Z0 and N0 avoids a case split when K is empty.
2. Bilinear bound. Let C_A := ||A||, the operator norm of A as a continuous linear map L -> L*. Then C_A >= 0 and |A[P][P']| <= C_A ||P|| ||P'|| for all P, P' in L (ContinuousLinearMap.le_opNorm₂; the norm on R is the absolute value). Lean note: to synthesize the norm on the bilinear-form type, put `set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3 in` before the theorem. The statement itself does not mention ||A||.
3. Claim (i): choice of k0. Fix eps > 0. Put C1 := (1 + r0^alpha)(N0 + 1) Z0 and C2 := C_A Z0; both are >= 0. Three facts hold for all sufficiently large k:
 a. |c_k| < (eps/2)/(C1 + 1), since c_k -> 0;
 b. ||U_k(z) - V(z)|| < min(1, (eps/2)/(C2 + 1)) for all z in K, since U_k -> V uniformly on K;
 c. the coefficient bound holds for every z in K, by hypothesis.
 Choose k0 such that a, b and c hold for every k >= k0.
4. Fix k >= k0 and z in K. Write P := U_k(z) and Q' := Q(z). By 3b, ||P - V(z)|| < 1, so ||P|| <= ||V(z)|| + ||P - V(z)|| <= N0 + 1.
5. Decomposition. A is linear in its first argument, so A[P][Q'] - A[V(z)][Q'] = A[P - V(z)][Q'] (map_sub, then evaluation of a difference of linear forms at Q'). Hence A[V(z)][Q'] - ah_k(z)[P][Q'] = -((ah_k(z)[P][Q'] - A[P][Q']) + A[P - V(z)][Q']).
6. First term. The coefficient bound gives |ah_k(z)[P][Q'] - A[P][Q']| <= c_k (1 + |z|^alpha) ||P|| ||Q'||. The factors 1 + |z|^alpha, ||P|| and ||Q'|| are >= 0, so this is <= |c_k| (1 + |z|^alpha) ||P|| ||Q'||. By steps 1 and 4 that is <= |c_k| (1 + r0^alpha)(N0 + 1) Z0 = |c_k| C1. By 3a, |c_k| C1 <= (eps/2) C1/(C1 + 1) < eps/2.
7. Second term. By step 2, |A[P - V(z)][Q']| <= C_A ||P - V(z)|| ||Q'|| <= C_A ||P - V(z)|| Z0 = ||P - V(z)|| C2. By 3b this is <= (eps/2) C2/(C2 + 1) < eps/2.
8. Steps 5 to 7 and the triangle inequality give |A[V(z)][Q(z)] - ah_k(z)[U_k(z)][Q(z)]| < eps/2 + eps/2 = eps for every k >= k0 and every z in K. Since eps > 0 was arbitrary, claim (i) holds.
9. Claim (ii). Fix eps > 0 and put C3 := r0^alpha Z0 >= 0. Since d_k -> 0 and the bound on Psi_k holds eventually, there is k1 such that every k >= k1 satisfies |d_k| < eps/(C3 + 1) and |Psi_k(z)[P]| <= d_k |z|^alpha ||P|| for all z in K and P in L. For such k and z in K, step 1 gives |0 - Psi_k(z)[Q(z)]| = |Psi_k(z)[Q(z)]| <= d_k |z|^alpha ||Q(z)|| <= |d_k| |z|^alpha ||Q(z)|| <= |d_k| r0^alpha Z0 = |d_k| C3 <= eps C3/(C3 + 1) < eps. Hence z -> Psi_k(z)[Q(z)] converges to 0 uniformly on K. QED.
proof_key_steps: nonnegative constants r0, Z0, N0 with |z|^alpha <= r0^alpha, ||Q(z)|| <= Z0, ||V(z)|| <= N0 on K, and C_A = ||A|| with |A[P][P']| <= C_A ||P|| ||P'||
given eps > 0, eventually |c_k| < (eps/2)/(C1+1), ||U_k - V|| < min(1, (eps/2)/(C2+1)) on K, and the coefficient bound holds on K
A[V][Q] - ah_k[U_k][Q] = -((ah_k - A)[U_k][Q] + A[U_k - V][Q]), with ||U_k|| <= N0 + 1
each of the two terms is < eps/2, so the pairings converge uniformly on K
|Psi_k(z)[Q(z)]| <= |d_k| r0^alpha Z0 < eps eventually, so the error forms converge uniformly to 0 on K

audit.reason: The standalone type matches every quantified bound and both conclusions. Nonnegative maxima handle unrestricted r, Z and N, including empty K. Absolute values correctly handle signed c and d. Bilinearity gives the stated decomposition, and the two epsilon/2 estimates and error estimate establish uniform convergence. Real-power monotonicity covers alpha=0. The operator-norm bound checks with synthesis depth 3; the frozen type itself needs no implementation or alias.

subproblem.title: Convergence of integrals under uniform convergence on a compact set containing the supports
subproblem.statement: Let n be a natural number; integrals are Bochner integrals for Lebesgue measure on R^n. Let K be a compact subset of R^n, f_k : R^n -> R (k in N) and g : R^n -> R. Assume: f_k is integrable for all sufficiently large k; g is integrable; for all sufficiently large k, f_k(z) = 0 for every z not in K; g(z) = 0 for every z not in K; and f_k -> g uniformly on K as k -> infinity. Then the integral of f_k over R^n tends to the integral of g over R^n as k -> infinity.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (K : Set (Rn n)) (f : ℕ → Rn n → ℝ) (g : Rn n → ℝ), IsCompact K → (∀ᶠ k in atTop, Integrable (f k)) → Integrable g → (∀ᶠ k in atTop, ∀ z, z ∉ K → f k z = 0) → (∀ z, z ∉ K → g z = 0) → TendstoUniformlyOn f g atTop K → Tendsto (fun k => ∫ z, f k z) atTop (𝓝 (∫ z, g z))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 4 and 5d of the parent proof (bounding an integral over the ball Bbar_r(0) that contains all supports), stated for a general compact set K. Let mu denote Lebesgue measure on R^n; all integrals are Bochner integrals for mu.
1. Finite measure. K is compact and mu is finite on compact sets, so mu(K) < infinity (IsCompact.measure_lt_top). Let M := mu(K) as a real number (M = mu.real K). Then M >= 0.
2. Choice of k0. Fix eps > 0 and put delta := eps / (M + 1) > 0. Uniform convergence on K in its metric form (Metric.tendstoUniformlyOn_iff) gives, for all sufficiently large k, |g(z) - f_k(z)| < delta for every z in K. Combine this with the two eventual hypotheses. This gives k0 such that every k >= k0 satisfies: (i) f_k is integrable; (ii) f_k(z) = 0 for all z not in K; (iii) |f_k(z) - g(z)| < delta for all z in K.
3. Fix k >= k0. Since f_k and g are integrable, the integral of f_k minus the integral of g equals the integral of f_k - g (integral_sub).
4. By (ii) and the hypothesis on g, f_k - g vanishes at every z not in K. So its integral over R^n equals its integral over K (setIntegral_eq_integral_of_forall_compl_eq_zero).
5. By (iii), |f_k(z) - g(z)| <= delta for every z in K, and mu(K) < infinity. Hence the absolute value of the integral of f_k - g over K is at most delta * M (norm_setIntegral_le_of_norm_le_const).
6. delta * M = eps * M / (M + 1) < eps, because M >= 0 and eps > 0 give eps * M < eps * (M + 1).
7. Steps 3 to 6 give |integral of f_k - integral of g| < eps for every k >= k0. Since eps > 0 was arbitrary, the integrals of f_k tend to the integral of g (Metric.tendsto_nhds). QED.
